exemplars.what: The title-page inscription of The Lord of the Rings, in Tolkien's own hand
exemplars.script: cirth and tengwar, one continuous inscription in two alphabets
exemplars.text: THE LORD OF THE RINGS TRANSLATED FROM THE RED BOOK | of Westmarch by John Ronald Reuel Tolkien herein is set forth the history of the War of the Ring and the return of the King as seen by the Hobbits
exemplars.mode: NOT ESTABLISHED for the tengwar half. The Reader's Companion names the two alphabets and not the tengwar MODE, and the mode in question is the English one whose letter values arda_tengwar_mode_gu.json declines to publish. For the CIRTH half it IS established and is a surprise: the Companion says the title-page cirth 'differs slightly from the Dwarvish Angerthas Moria as described in Appendix E, but is essentially consistent with the usage of Erebor'.
exemplars.note: WHICH HALF IS IN WHICH SCRIPT IS NOT WHAT A CASUAL LOOK SUGGESTS, and both corpus witnesses agree against the casual look: the FIRST line -- 'THE LORD OF THE RINGS TRANSLATED FROM THE RED BOOK' -- is the runic CIRTH, and the TENGWAR carries the remainder. The two witnesses disagree on one word: the Companion has 'the War of the Ring' and t3_lotr_1954_2004 has 'the War of the RingS'. The lower tier wins, so the singular stands and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved silently. The Companion also records that Tolkien 'made minor errors in the lettering' of the first edition, corrected in the first printing of The Return of the King and the second printings of the other two -- so the inscription is not one text but two states of one text.

unestablished.what they are: Read as images: two-line bands of CURSIVE tengwar set between double rules. The letterforms are the same hand as the tengwar half of the LotR title-page inscription, and the words are plainly English rather than Quenya -- there are no long carriers and no doubled tehtar where a Quenya text would need them. [I-M], a reading of a picture.
unestablished.why no transcription: THE ARCHIVE HAS NO TABLE TO READ THEM WITH. They are English in tengwar, and site/arda_tengwar_mode_gu.json's `unresolved` block records that the General Use consonant chart on Amanye Tenceli is an IMAGE with empty alt text and that Appendix E's tables are images in the edition this archive holds. Transcribing them would mean inventing about thirty letter values and then reading a picture through them. Not attempted.
unestablished.what the corpus DOES say about the Silma: It describes a DIFFERENT jacket. `t2_pictures_by_j_r_r_tolkien.txt:708-709` records that 'the second device of Luthien Tinuviel' appeared 'on the jacket of The Silmarillion' -- Tolkien's own heraldic device, not a tengwar band. So the bands the owner supplied belong to a LATER edition the corpus does not document, and the archive cannot even name which edition. [C] on what the corpus says; the rest is unestablished.
unestablished.what would settle it: A published letter-by-letter reading of these specific bands, or the General Use / English-mode value table from a source the archive may read as TEXT rather than as a GIF. Mellonath Daeron's DTS index is the obvious place; it was not reachable in this turn.
unestablished.what was tried: The corpus was searched through ardatext for every phrasing of a jacket description this session could think of. The web research that would have closed it did not complete: the session's search budget was exhausted and the delegated agent was terminated by a content filter before reporting.

direction.owner: 19 August 2026: 'the edges of the leafs have some minimal art, replace them with real tengwar, cirth, and sarati scripts, which always should be relevant to the currently opened pages'
direction.exemplars: uploads/scripts/LOTR.jpg, Silmarillion-1.jpg, Silmarillion-2.jpg, Unfinished-Tales-1.jpg, Unfinished-Tales-2.jpg -- two-line tengwar bands between double rules. Their LOOK is what this dataset is set to; their TEXT is English in tengwar and is recorded in `exemplars`, not reproduced -- see `refuses`.

refuses.sarati: REFUSED, and not for want of a font. The archive holds Tirion Sarati and 48 CSUR sarati glyphs and NO sound-to-glyph binding: site/arda_sarati_keyboard.json refuses it in its own words, and site/arda_sarati_tirion.json -- the shape-matching bridge that would supply it -- has never been written. Sarati shapes can be drawn here and cannot be read, so none are written.
refuses.english in tengwar: REFUSED. The five cover bands the owner points at are English in tengwar, and site/arda_tengwar_mode_gu.json declares that the archive will not publish the General Use letter values it cannot cite. Reproducing a band would mean inventing them.
refuses.sindarin in tengwar: REFUSED. The Mode of Beleriand is described in Appendix E and its vowel values are never stated there; arda_cirth.json's own `refused` block says so. Sindarin names go into the Angerthas Daeron, which App E does assign to Sindarin.
refuses.a letter with no certh: REFUSED per route and named. The Angerthas Daeron as read from the plate carries no h and no y; the Angerthas Erebor carries no unambiguous s. Those are Tolkien's tables, not this module's shortfall.

cirth.font: fonts/AngerthasMoria.woff2 is an ASCII-mapped face and is NOT used here; the CSUR faces are fonts/TengwarTelcontar.woff2 (49 of the 128 cirth codepoints, outline) and fonts/ArdaCSUR.woff2 (128 of 128, a 16x16 BITMAP at 64 units/em). Telcontar first, CSUR after.

tengwar.font: fonts/TengwarTelcontar.woff2, fonts/AlcarinTengwar-Regular.woff2, fonts/Eldamar-1.1.woff2 -- all three CSUR-encoded and all three carrying a recorded licence in site/arda_assets.json

n(r).why: certh 12; the parenthesis is the Dwarves' value-shift to r, which the Moria and Erebor columns carry separately. Daeron reads n.

ŋ (n).why: certh 22; ŋ is not a Latin letter this transcriber accepts, and the parenthesised n would collide with certh 12. DROPPED rather than chosen.

z (ss).why: certh 36; App E gives a theoretic z used for ss in Elvish. z is primary.

i (y).why: certh 39; App E states this value in prose. i is primary, y secondary.

(mh) mb.why: certh 7; the bracketed mh is the archaic spirant. mb is the stated value.

ks (x).why: certh 17, Erebor; x is the Latin spelling of the same sound.

' (glottal).why: certh 35, Moria/Erebor; the Khuzdul glottal beginning has no Latin letter in a name as this archive spells names. DROPPED.

s*.why: certh 54, Erebor; the star is this archive's own mark that the value is WEAK -- 54 is one of the six weak rows in arda_cirth_codepoints. DROPPED.

n*.why: certh 53, Moria; weak, and App E notes confusion with 22. DROPPED.

+h*.why: certh 59, Moria; a modifier, not a letter. DROPPED.

+h.why: certh 59, Erebor; a modifier, not a letter. DROPPED.

ə*.why: certh 55, Moria; a vowel with no Latin spelling here. DROPPED.

&*.why: certh 60, Moria; an ampersand is not a letter. DROPPED.

—.why: the arrangement assigns no value to this certh.
